summary: Session S4 exhaustively analyzed all approaches (strong induction on k, nf_agreement_monotone, nf_fraisse_compression, game-based). Confirmed S3 root cause: interval_nf_types loses spatial info. Key finding: even with strong induction and nf_agreement_monotone, the sub-interval ordering problem persists because zone-matched interior points lack mutual ordering constraints. Three sorries remain (2347, 2429, 2787). Resolution requires enriched 3-var interval types (~400-600 lines).

blocking_issues.description: Bridge lemma's interval_nf_types hypothesis is semantically too weak for the 4-var existential transfer. All non-enrichment approaches fail.
blocking_issues.root_cause: Zone matching against 2-point boundary (x,t) gives correct orderings with x and t but NOT with other zone-matched interior points. When two interior points are in the same sub-interval, their relative ordering is undetermined. This blocks 4-var NF agreement even at depth 0 (atoms include orderings between all 4 vars).
approaches_exhausted: Strong induction on k: IH at depth j < k gives 2-var bridge, need 3-var. Generalizing to n-var fails because IH needs sub-interval types for extended configs.
nf_agreement_monotone: gives multi-depth transfer from shared NF, but depth-k 1-var NF agreement does NOT imply multi-var NF agreement.
nf_fraisse_compression: atoms OK but existential transfer at each depth re-encounters the ordering problem.

Game approach: correct in principle but requires ExtendedCarrier<->M.carrier type bridge, rank_type<->nf_characteristic bridge, and formula_agreement<->NF_agreement via char_k. Significant infrastructure cost.
Pairwise 2-var agreements: from depth-k 1-var NFs, get depth-(k-1) 2-var transfer for each pair, but different pairs give DIFFERENT witnesses that may not be consistent.

changes_made.description: Exhaustive analysis of all approaches with detailed failure modes

resolution_plan.rationale: A 3-var interval type sigma = nf_characteristic M k 3 (u, x, t) encodes: (a) u's orderings with BOTH x and t, (b) u's predicates, (c) depth-(k-1) 4-var quantifier data for extensions of (u,x,t). Zone matching with 3-var types gives u' with ALL orderings and ALL quantifier data, fully resolving the sub-interval ordering problem.
steps: 1. Define interval_3var_nf_types M k lo hi: Finset of depth-k 3-var NFs for (u, lo, hi) with u in (lo, hi). ~30 lines.
2. Prove depth decrease for 3-var interval types. ~50 lines.
3. New zone_match_3var: from interval_3var_nf_types equality, find u' with matching 3-var NF. ~60-90 lines.

4. New nf_2var_existential_transfer using 3-var zone match: From 3-var NF agreement at depth k, get depth-j 3-var agreement by monotonicity, extract quantifier for depth-j 4-var transfer. ~80-120 lines.
5. Modify nf_exist_sf_guarded formula to encode enriched interval types (requires char_2var from completeness IH or Classical.choice). ~80-120 lines.
6. Re-prove forward/backward directions. Forward: straightforward. Backward: extract 3-var interval types from formula guard. ~80-120 lines.
resolution_plan.key_insight: From 3-var NF agreement at depth k (via 3-var zone match): nf_agreement_monotone gives depth-j' 3-var agreement for j' < k. The depth-j' 3-var NF quantifier part at depth j'-1 gives (j'-1)-level 4-var transfer. Combined with atoms at 3 vars (from 3-var NF): nf_fraisse_compression at depth j' gives 3-var NF at depth j'. The quantifier at depth j'-1 gives the j'-level 4-var existential transfer needed by the sorry goals.
resolution_plan.caution: Step 5 (formula encoding) may have circular dependency: the formula needs to characterize 3-var NFs, which requires the completeness theorem at higher var count. Resolution: use Classical.choice or encode only 1-var interval types in the formula and derive 3-var types from 1-var types + bridge lemma IH.
